History: The Avites were one of the Mesopotamian peoples Assyria resettled in Samaria after Israel's fall (2 Kings 17:24). They made Nibhaz and Tartak their gods (2 Kings 17:31). They are not the Avvim of Deuteronomy 2:23, a different people near Gaza displaced by the Caphtorim — the similar names cover two different groups.
Culture: As a Mesopotamian people, the Avites shared the urban culture of Babylon's world; nothing further is recorded of them.
Religion: The Avites worshipped Nibhaz and Tartak, gods they carried with them to Samaria.
BibleConnection: The Avites appear only in the resettlement list and its note on their gods — one more strand in the mixed population that became Samaria.
